report.headline: Usage projected to climb above the EuroLeague average, but the shooting projection carries no signal

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to rise from 16.1% in the 2013-14 NBA season to 22.2% in the EuroLeague, above the league's minutes-weighted average of 20.4%.

risks.text: The true shooting projection of 56.3% should not be trusted: its held-out error (4.7% MAE) is no better than simply guessing the EuroLeague average, so it carries no information about this player.
Even for usage, the 80% interval (18.0%-26.4%) and 95% interval (15.8%-28.6%) are wide relative to the league's spread (SD 4.2%), covering a large swath of plausible EuroLeague roles.

The player's NBA usage rate sat 0.82 standard deviations below the league average, a notably lower starting point than the -0.31 sd average for players who historically made this same move, making the comparison less typical of the fitted cohort.
The estimate rests on 115 historical NBA-to-EuroLeague transitions, a moderate but not extensive sample.

strengths.text: Usage rate is projected to rise to 22.2%, above the EuroLeague average of 20.4%, driven by a fitted slope of 0.982 — meaning almost all of the player's standing above their NBA peers is expected to carry over.
The usage rate model beats a trivial league-mean baseline (3.3% MAE vs 4.3%), so this particular projection carries real signal.
In the source season the player combined a low turnover rate (12.2%) with a heavily three-point-oriented shot profile (49.0% of attempts from three).

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate (18.0%-26.4%) spans roughly two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution (SD 4.2%), so the model can rank this player relative to peers but cannot pin down an individual value; the true shooting projection (56.3%) should be treated as uninformative since the model's error there (4.7% MAE) is no better than a league-mean baseline (4.7%).
